Telescopes gather light from distant stars and galaxies. A larger telescope
aperture collects more photons, letting astronomers observe fainter nebulae.

The parallax method measures stellar distances by observing how a nearby star
appears to shift against background galaxies as the Earth orbits the Sun.

Radio telescopes detect emissions from pulsars and quasars, objects invisible
to optical astronomy. Interferometry combines many antennas into one giant
virtual telescope with extraordinary angular resolution.
